displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest historical-resurrection case is cumulative: early conviction, retained local knowledge, partially independent attestation, and resistant narrative features jointly favor an unusual originating event beyond ordinary bereavement experiences.

novelty.explanation: This replaces several individually underdetermined inferences with an explicitly cumulative and proportionate historical claim.

premises.text: Historical rarity should lower an event’s prior probability, but it should not impose a fixed ceiling that prevents sufficiently discriminating evidence from increasing the posterior probability.

novelty.explanation: It formalizes the methodological challenge while expressly conceding the skeptical force of rarity.

premises.text: Local geography, period-appropriate names, and potentially earlier composition support continuity only within their demonstrated domains and should not independently certify every saying or episode.

novelty.explanation: It narrows the documentary inference to avoid sliding from local knowledge to comprehensive reliability.

premises.text: Gospel contradictions defeat strict inerrancy, yet fallible and mediated accounts may still retain a common historical core when variations do not erase shared central claims.

novelty.explanation: It incorporates the strongest contradiction objection while preserving a bounded continuity argument.

premises.text: A natural explanation must account jointly for initial experiences, bodily interpretation, continuing doubt, persuasion, missionary action, and rapid theological reframing rather than explaining only the first visionary episode.

novelty.explanation: It answers the stronger multistage skeptical model rather than a simplified bereavement analogy.

premises.text: Narrative awkwardness counts modestly for experiential residue only when the relevant features resist both smooth advocacy and plausible layered literary purposes; oddity alone is insufficient.

novelty.explanation: It adds a comparative criterion missing from the original appeal to narrative strangeness.

conclusion.text: If the documentary continuity, common core, explanatory shortfall of ordinary alternatives, and comparatively resistant details survive source-specific testing, a bodily-resurrection hypothesis deserves serious historical consideration without being treated as conclusively established.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion is deliberately conditional and avoids claiming more certainty than the cumulative premises support.

newArguments.title: Discriminating-evidence test
newArguments.text: Instead of counting reports, compare what each hypothesis predicts. A bodily encounter may predict durable conviction alongside shock, doubt, tactile checking, and difficulty describing continuity and transformation. A vision-plus-development model may predict visionary conviction and later bodily elaboration. The pro case improves only if the earliest recoverable evidence contains the first cluster before the proposed polemical pressures could readily generate it. This test converts narrative strangeness from an intuition into a comparative research program and permits the skeptical hypothesis to prevail when the chronology runs the other way.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a hypothesis-prediction framework not stated in any locked participant move.

newArguments.title: Correlated-cost caution
newArguments.text: The skeptical explanation invokes several ordinary mechanisms: visions, persuasion, reinterpretation, oral change, literary dependence, and polemical development. Those mechanisms cannot simply be multiplied as independent advantages, because some may be correlated or require specific sequencing. A cumulative pro case can ask whether the full natural reconstruction becomes less economical once timing, social transmission, bodily interpretation, and resistant details are jointly constrained. This does not prove resurrection; it identifies a fair comparative burden that evaluates complete causal packages rather than contrasting one extraordinary claim with an unpriced collection of ordinary possibilities.

novelty.explanation: This adds a causal-model complexity argument while expressly limiting its historical conclusion.

thesis.text: The strongest skeptical case grants genuine experiences and some preserved history while arguing that dependent sources, ordinary visionary processes, social reinterpretation, and later polemical shaping better explain the record than a historically established bodily resurrection.

novelty.explanation: This integrates the separate skeptical moves into one cumulative model without presuming fabrication or impossibility.

premises.text: The Gospels are not four fully independent witness statements: literary dependence, anonymous narration, later composition, and Johannine distinctiveness require tradition-by-tradition source analysis.

novelty.explanation: It translates general source criticism into a requirement for claim-specific independence analysis.

premises.text: Concrete contradictions demonstrate authorial selection or alteration, though their proper consequence is bounded confidence in disputed details rather than dismissal of every historical claim.

novelty.explanation: It preserves the original argument’s narrow entailment and calibrated baseline.

premises.text: Extraordinary reports may gain probability from evidence, but historians must compare actual independence and reliability with mistake, dependence, invention, and interpretive development instead of applying either automatic acceptance or rejection.

novelty.explanation: It removes the suggestion of an absolute historical ceiling while retaining comparative method.

premises.text: A few sincere post-crucifixion experiences could initiate belief without every follower sharing the same experience, because persuasion and prior messianic commitment can diffuse conviction through a group.

novelty.explanation: It makes the social transmission step explicit and avoids requiring uniform collective visions.

premises.text: Bodily scenes can preserve inherited material while also being amplified or arranged to answer later disputes, so polemical function need not imply wholesale literary invention.

novelty.explanation: It accommodates the strongest experiential-trace objection and distinguishes adaptation from creation.

conclusion.text: Because the ordinary reconstruction explains sincere conviction, theological transformation, documentary variation, and bodily narrative development without denying every historical core, the surviving evidence does not historically establish a bodily resurrection.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion integrates the skeptical route and remains limited to historical establishment.

newArguments.title: Chronological layering test
newArguments.text: The skeptical case can be made testable by ordering the evidence rather than merely labeling scenes late. First identify the earliest recoverable claims; then track when empty-tomb detail, tactile verification, eating, misrecognition, and supernatural movement become textually visible. If increasingly concrete bodily demonstrations appear alongside identifiable controversies over spiritual resurrection, development gains explanatory support. If the complete awkward cluster is independently early, that support weakens. This chronological test answers the objection that polemical usefulness does not prove invention and prevents source criticism from becoming a generic explanation applied regardless of sequence.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an explicit chronological prediction capable of supporting or weakening literary development.

newArguments.title: Network-diffusion model
newArguments.text: A new movement does not require many identical founding experiences. A small number of high-trust visionaries can influence close associates; shared messianic expectations provide interpretive vocabulary; communal rehearsal stabilizes selected claims; missionary success then rewards portable formulations. This network model predicts sincere conviction, uneven doubt, and rapid spread without treating participants as deceptive or psychologically uniform. Its force depends on evidence for authority relationships and communication pathways, but it directly addresses the claim that ordinary bereavement experiences cannot plausibly set a durable religion in motion.

novelty.explanation: This adds a social-network mechanism absent from the locked visionary and reinterpretation moves.
